summary.headline: Cohance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 23% YoY to INR4,223 million and adjusted EBITDA margin dropped to 2.2%, with management guiding to a Q2 sequential rebound.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was management's stated lowest quarter ever, driven by shipment phasing in Pharma CDMO (down 38.7% YoY), a weak agrochemicals quarter, low formulation revenue and NJ Bio underperformance. Sapala grew 2.5x YoY and the standalone business delivered a 9.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, but NJ Bio's INR328 million adjusted EBITDA loss weighed on the consolidated numbers. Management guided to sequential improvement in Q2 FY27, YoY growth from H2 FY27, and margin recovery weighted to H2. Adjusted EBITDA of INR92 million and gross margin of 71.5% (vs 73%) reflected negative operating leverage. Management also laid out an integrated nucleic acid business under Dr. P.Y. Reddy with a path to full Sapala ownership by FY30, and disclosed a USFDA Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram.

segments.name: Pharma CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 38.7% YoY on shipment phasing; commercial OTIF near 100% YTD and commercial vs development mix 57:43. Restocking order received for one molecule that destocked last year, with visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: API+ (API and formulations)
segments.commentary: API performed slightly ahead of internal expectations on favourable pricing and mix. Formulations were below expectations on an API production delay, lower demand for a mature product and a pack configuration change; Nacharam supplies have resumed but remediation continues.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 34.7% YoY, led by H2-skewed AgChem phasing; Performance materials grew and were in line with plan. Two Japanese innovator qualification campaigns are scheduled in FY27.

segments.name: ADC / NJ Bio
segments.commentary: Revenue INR350 million with adjusted EBITDA loss of INR328 million. Some payload deliveries moved from Q1 into later quarters; FTE renewals are at risk from biotech funding conditions.

segments.name: Sapala (oligonucleotides)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR274 million, 2.5x YoY, after supply began on a specialised nucleic acid building blocks programme; EBITDA margin described as strong.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 to show sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA, with movement toward YoY comparability by end of H1 and YoY growth from H2 FY27.
Margin recovery weighted to H2 FY27; CFO expects Q2 FY27 margin in line with prior-year margin percentage for the current year, accelerating from FY28.
Pharma CDMO: two molecules moved into commercial supply, with six intermediates scheduled for delivery across Q2 and Q3 FY27; customized ADC payload order on schedule for Q2 FY27.
API+: targeting seven new API filings in FY27 and around 10 formulation launches this fiscal year, with two in Q2 FY27.
Management views the USD 1 billion FY30 revenue target as an aspiration; will provide an update by December.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR598 million in Q1 FY27 to support future growth.
Commercial flow reactor at Jaggayyapet expected to be ready next quarter.
New effluent treatment facility commissioned at Ankleshwar; several API debottlenecking projects completed.
Commercialising the new amidites facility and operationalising Sapala's GMP oligonucleotide facility, with validation of priority amidites in progress.
Additional GMP manufacturing laboratory operationalised at Princeton for NJ Bio; another GMP ADC batch released.
Evaluating targeted capacity additions across small molecules, ADCs, API+ and specialty chemicals; Specialty Chemicals R&D, manufacturing and asset strategy being finalised.
demand_pricing: Pharma CDMO RFQ pipeline strengthened, with Phase 3 KSM commercial inquiries from a large pharma company; clients typically have one or two existing sources, which slows conversion.
Ten molecules in Phase 3 pipeline per management; more than 50% are expected to get approval.
Two commercial molecules face patent expiry, but the intermediates supplied are for post-expiry products and revenue impact was already seen in the past two fiscal years.
API+ price increases passed through a major part of raw material escalations, largely in Q4 FY26; API order book described as robust.
Customers in ADC payloads show positive response to MMAE and Exatecan, which are gaining traction as alternatives to Chinese suppliers.
Two CEP approvals obtained and two Korean DMFs filed during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Growth ranges by segment over 2-3 years and beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Umang Vohra said nucleic acid CDMO could roughly double within 3-4 years, API+ could be a CAGR business and perhaps only 30-40% of its potential, and most growth becomes visible from H2 FY27. He stressed these were directional, not strategic plan targets.

qa_highlights.name: Macro and Indian CDMO RFQ trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Yann D'Herve said geopolitical diversification and US de-risking are increasing late-stage RFQs, but conversion is slow because clients already have one or two sources.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook beyond FY27 after NJ Bio and Sapala changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said margins should rise steadily YoY with operating leverage; whether they reach 35% is hard to say. Later, he guided Q2 FY27 margin close to the prior-year level and acceleration from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Restocking contribution from the INR260 crore destocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said it is too early to quantify the restocking, since the order for one molecule is spread over two years; clarity is expected by the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses trend and merger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said there were no merger-related or one-off costs in Q1; the expenses are administrative and recurring and should be assumed to continue through the year.

risks_watch: NJ Bio: INR328 million adjusted EBITDA loss in Q1; management says it will keep weighing on consolidated profit until revenue conversion improves, and FTE renewals are at risk from biotech funding conditions.
Q2 FY27 delivery slippage: some Pharma CDMO and ADC payload deliveries moved from Q1 into later quarters, so the guided sequential Q2 rebound depends on timely execution.
Restocking visibility: the INR260 crore destocking is not yet quantified; the order for one molecule is spread over two years, with clarity promised by the next call.
Nacharam remediation and formulation recovery; new USFDA Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram (inspection 27 July to 5 August 2026) to be answered within timelines.
CFO transition: Himanshu Agarwal remains until 13 September 2026, with succession still to be announced. Management will update on the USD 1 billion FY30 target by December.
key_quotes: As we had indicated in our previous earnings call, Q1 of this year would be our lowest quarter ever, and that is how the quarter has played out.
Certain deliveries moved from Q1FY27 into Q2FY27, and are now on track for delivery this quarter.
At this point, I am almost feeling like that the target is an aspiration.
So we should be looking at a number which will be closer to previous year margin percentage for the current year. And we should thereafter start accelerating from FY28 onwards.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on the recovery path in directional terms, but cautious on quantification: it repeatedly declined to size FY27 restocking, gave no segment-level revenue numbers, and called the USD 1 billion FY30 target an aspiration. Margin commentary is specific only for Q2 (close to prior-year margin percentage) and vague beyond FY28.
